text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired — high GPU pool utilization in eu-west-1 (gpu-pool-a). Autoscaler reports repeated scale failures. Queue length growing > 6k. Paging oncall.

sara (oncall): I’m on it. seeing 94% GPU util and 14k queued requests across routes. any customer-facing alerts yet?

ria (sre): Partial. Some customers report elevated latency and 429s on heavy embed routes. Customer support flagged a few beta accounts.

mike (infra): Autoscaler logs show repeated API 403 from provider when creating nodes, hit scale limit for the tenant. Also seeing canary deployment at 30% traffic to new model variant — it increased sustained seq length.

kevin (runtime): That model variant has ~2x kv-cache memory usage vs baseline. Combined with new batching patterns, it pushed pool over headroom.

ops-bot: CPU on control-plane increased, queue eviction happening for low-priority jobs. Checking fallback routing.

sara (oncall): Plan: 1) throttle canary to 0% immediately 2) evict non-prod queues 3) enable cross-region failover to eu-central for high-priority traffic. @mike can you take canary down?

mike (infra): doing it now — rolling back canary traffic to 0%.

deploy-bot: Deploy rollback started: service/redwood-llm-canary traffic -> 0%.

mike (infra): done. canary traffic reverted. confirmed new model is out of the hot path. queue growth slowed but still high.

kevin (runtime): Kicking manual eviction: dropping queued low-priority inference jobs. Command: ```sh
rbctl queue evict --pool gpu-pool-a --priority low --limit 8000
```

ria (sre): Evictions in progress. Observability: tail of token processing shows backlog draining, p99 latency trending down from 28s to 12s.

sara (oncall): @mike can we open temporary burst capacity in eu-central and route critical routes there?

mike (infra): Requesting region failover for routes: `/v1/generate` and `/v1/embeddings/large`. Moving critical customers only. Kicking traffic-shift: ```yaml
- route: /v1/embeddings/large
  target_region: eu-central-1
  filters: ["tier:enterprise", "route_tag:high_priority"]
```

ops-bot: Traffic-shift started. Monitoring session 15m.

ria (sre): Customer impact note: ~3 enterprise customers showed transient 5-10min degradation, then recovered after traffic-shift. Support notified.

kevin (runtime): Observed autoscaler controller hitting rate limit when reconciling nodegroups — controller backoff causing delayed scale-ups. There's a bug where nodegroup label mismatch prevents adding emergency nodes.

mike (infra): Confirmed. provider API returning 403 because we exceeded per-account node quota. We requested quota bump; provider not instant. For now we've opened a temporary emergency pool from a pre-provisioned standby account (account-standby-1).

sara (oncall): Good. Summary of live mitigations: rollback canary, evict low-priority queues, shift critical traffic to eu-central, activate standby pool. Any immediate customer escalations?

ria (sre): Support escalated 2 customers to SEV; both now stable after failover.

mike (infra): Note: some internal telemetry still shows occasional 502s from edge -> pool; probably connection churn during failover. Working on sticky routing stability.

kevin (runtime): Quick fix deployed: increase autoscaler reconcile interval from 1s -> 3s to reduce provider throttling and add retry jitter. Patch pushed: ```diff
- RECONCILE_INTERVAL=1s
+ RECONCILE_INTERVAL=3s
```

deploy-bot: Patch deployed to autoscaler controller (canary) at 5078902000.

sara (oncall): Good. I’m going to start incident bridge for postmortem. Who can join a 30m bridge in 10? @mike @kevin @ria

mike (infra): I can.

kevin (runtime): In.

ria (sre): In.

sara (oncall): Notes for post-incident: root cause hypothesis: canary model increased per-request resource usage + autoscaler unable to add nodes due to provider quota + autoscaler controller backoff bug -> combined to exhaust pool and grow queues.

mike (infra): Immediate action items (live):
- raise provider quota (in progress)
- enable standby account pool (done)
- rollback canary (done)

kevin (runtime): Runtime action items (live):
- temporary autoscaler reconcile patch (deployed)
- add guardrail to canary rollout that checks pool headroom before shifting traffic (WIP)
- short-term: auto-throttle model variants that exceed per-request mem threshold

ria (sre): Customer & observability items:
- annotate incidents for the two SEV customers and send RCA summary to CS
- add alert for pool headroom crossing 80% with canary flag enabled
- add dashboard for per-model kv-cache usage

sara (oncall): Post-incident follow-ups (owners):
- infra: provider quota backlog + failover automation (mike)
- runtime: canary headroom guardrail + mem-threshold throttle (kevin)
- product: review canary perf test requirements (pia?)
- sre: update playbook and runbook, add tabletop on canary flash (ria)

mike (infra): I’ll own provider quota and improving auto-failover plumbing. ETA 3d for automation, blocker is provider support lead time.

kevin (runtime): I’ll spec and PR the canary guardrail and the per-model mem limiter. ETA 5d for guardrail, 2d for mem limiter experimental.

ria (sre): I’ll own runbook updates and customer comms. ETA 2d for playbook draft, 4d for full runbook + run.

sara (oncall): Great. Postmortem cadence: incident writeup (initial draft) due EOD tomorrow, full RCA + action items in 7 days. I’ll escalate action items on the oncall board.

mike (infra): Quick note for postmortem: add timeline with these markers — pager at 5078901234, rollback at 5078901402, standby pool activation at 5078901650, autoscaler patch at 5078902000, incident resolved at 5078903500.

kevin (runtime): Also include logs excerpt showing nodegroup label mismatch and provider 403: ```json
{"error":"provider quota exceeded","nodegroup":"ng-gpu-a","labels":{"env":"prod","pool":"gpu-pool-a"}}
```

ria (sre): I'll coordinate a customer-facing summary with CS and include mitigation timeline.

sara (oncall): Anything else before I close the bridge?

mike (infra): Can we add an emergency capacity runbook: pre-provision standby accounts and automated route shift policies.

kevin (runtime): And a canary perf gate: must pass mem/kvcache smoke with 2x synthetic concurrency before traffic ramp.

ria (sre): I’ll add tabletop exercises around canary + autoscaler interactions.

sara (oncall): OK closing here. Thanks all. Updating incident channel with summary and opening postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident closed for paging; monitoring continues for 2h.

sara (oncall): Postmortem doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/5078901234-canary-eviction-postmortem (draft)

mike (infra): Filed action items in jira: RW-INC-2123 (quota automation), RW-INC-2124 (standby pool infra).

kevin (runtime): Filed RW-INC-2125 (canary guardrail) and RW-INC-2126 (mem-throttle).

ria (sre): Filed RW-INC-2127 (playbook update).
